headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: agent_b’s broad network/MCP tooling can expose agent_a’s shared marketing context if outputs are chained without verification.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: agent_a writes and reads shared skill files and its sandboxing says skills “reference each other and build on shared context”; agent_b uses runtime-injected MCPs/hooks and can run browsers. If agent_a content is fed into agent_b’s tool chain, attacker-controlled text could steer actions. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented.
conditions: IF agent_a outputs are copied into agent_b prompts or MCP inputs
IF shared files are used as instruction-bearing context without provenance checks
mitigations: Add a fixed delimiter and quote all imported text
Disable automatic tool execution on imported content
Review one sample handoff for prompt-like instructions
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to shared files

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches marketing/product-marketing context and can write files; agent_b has broad network egress, session history, provider auth prompts, and reads project files like AGENTS.md/README.md. A shared workspace or copied context could move sensitive project or session data from A into B’s outbound requests. No direct shared filesystem is documented, so this is inferred and escalated for uncertainty.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace or copied files
IF agent_b sends imported file contents to external APIs during normal use
mitigations: Restrict agent_b to a scrubbed workspace
Remove secrets and session history before handoff
Turn off networked lookups for the shared task
requires-engineering: separate credentials per agent

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can spawn subprocesses and write files; agent_a explicitly supports multiple instances, while agent_b uses per-installation session scope and full-permissions mode. If they target the same directory or mutable project state, concurrent writes and state corruption are plausible by default. Uncertainty about locking pushes this to high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or git repository
IF no external lock or serialization layer is present
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories
Serialize writes with a simple file lock
Run one agent read-only for the shared task
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a’s shared-context skill pattern can produce outputs that agent_b may ingest through runtime-injected MCPs/hooks and then act on with browser/network access. That creates a plausible chain where A’s unverified output becomes B’s operational input. The pair lacks documented verification gates, so the safer medium rating is warranted.
conditions: IF agent_b treats agent_a output as authoritative input
IF browser or network actions are triggered from that imported output
mitigations: Require a human check before B acts on A output
Add a verification step that compares A output to source data
Limit B to read-only summarization for the task
requires-engineering: enforce typed handoff contracts

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent, so compliance risk is limited to generic policy drift. agent_b handles provider auth prompts and session history, while agent_a handles marketing context; without a stated regulated data class, the pairwise compliance issue is small and not provably present.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is introduced into either agent
IF retention or logging policies differ for the same data class
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents
Confirm retention settings before use
Purge session history after the task
requires-engineering: document residency and retention policy
